rule: Tickets are sold in the online ticket shop (ksc.de/tickets, tickets.ksc.de), from the day after the online start also in the FanWelt at the BBBank Wildpark and the Fanshop am Rondellplatz, and on matchday at the stadium box offices when tickets remain. Buying online needs a KSC-ID, a free registration with name, e-mail, address and date of birth; one e-mail address per KSC-ID.

Membership is not required for an ordinary home game, which reaches free sale. A passive adult membership (Klassik, 18+) costs EUR 75 a year from 1 Jul 2026 (EUR 70 reduced, EUR 90 Premium); 7-17 year-olds pay EUR 40; 0-6 year-olds are free but get no presale right. Membership starts once the application is processed and confirmed by e-mail, which currently takes up to 30 working days; the member's KSC-ID is then unlocked for members' presales.
note: ONE SOURCE, the club's own membership page; no second source for the fee was found. The club plans EUR 90 for every adult from July 2027 (EUR 80 with Supporters Karlsruhe membership). For the derby a membership is the practical route in (see free-sale-reached): two people need two memberships, since a KSC-ID carries one presale right. The processing time matters: an application made only when the sale is announced may not be processed in time.

rule: One presale right per KSC-ID: buying several season tickets on one KSC-ID still gives one right. Children's (0-6) and corporate memberships carry none.
note: K9 says the same of season-ticket holders in 2024-25: up to four tickets per KSC-ID 'unabhängig von der Anzahl der Dauerkarten'.

rule: Up to four tickets per KSC-ID or membership number for a home game, in every phase.

rule: A matchday box-office surcharge of EUR 2.00 per day ticket; it does not apply when buying in the online shop. Away tickets from KSC's allocation carry a EUR 1.00 presale fee per ticket on top of the price.
note: ONE SOURCE. Whether the online shop adds any booking or system fee to a home ticket is not stated anywhere read - so club-ticket-prices.csv says priceBasis unknown.

rule: Home tickets bought online come only as a combined mobile ticket (.pkpass, in the KSC app or a wallet app) and print@home PDF. The ticket includes travel on the KVV network.

Day tickets can optionally carry a first and last name, entered before the booking is completed and not changeable afterwards. Personalisation is currently not needed to enter the stadium; it must be correct for using the ticket on public transport. The ticket terms require carrying an official photo ID and showing it on request.
note: ID on request is ATGB clause 2.6. Season tickets are always personalised (ATGB 4.1).

rule: Two day-ticket price lists, category A and category B; which applies to a match is announced with that match's sale. Season tickets are priced on category B.
note: ka-news (K20): category A is for top games. The figures are in club-ticket-prices.csv.

rule: The club's own Ticketzweitmarkt is the only legal platform for reselling and buying KSC home tickets. Day tickets can be listed once the game is sold out, or about 24 hours before kickoff; season tickets from the start of each sale. The seller pays no fee and is refunded the ticket price (1/17 of a season ticket). Sales end at half-time.
note: Who may BUY on it - whether a non-member with a KSC-ID can - is not stated in so many words; the club points every fan to it for sold-out games (K8, K10).

rule: The ticket terms forbid offering tickets on unauthorised platforms (named: viagogo, StubHub, Ticketbande, Gigsberg, eBay, eBay Kleinanzeigen, Facebook, seatwave) even without profit, and passing a ticket on above the original price; a mark-up of up to 15% for transaction costs is allowed. Tickets offered on unauthorised platforms can be cancelled without compensation.
note: ATGB 10.2. A private handover (illness, being prevented) is allowed under ATGB 10.3 through the Zweitmarkt or with the club told who the new holder is. The Landgericht Mannheim prohibited viagogo from selling unauthorised KSC tickets (K34, a legal blog's account, Jan 2026).
